title: Three Days and One Short Ticket
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：wheel　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 wheel 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the driver ① turned the wheel that no passenger in the station would have counted, and he said the turning was the whole of the day. The ② wheel, meaning the ring itself and not the ticket, ran three days and stayed uncounted in the book; a wheel, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ wheel in that station had the same short ticket beside it, and the ④ wheel at the far platform, meaning the seat they kept for the children to book and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A wheel, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the driver said the counting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the wheel was the whole of the matter, meaning the motion and not the ring. The ⑥ wheel, meaning the motion and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; wheel, he said, is either something you turn or the only word that means both a ring and a motion. He said the motion is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ wheel had become a line in a timetable, and the timetable had become an argument about the short ticket. The ⑧ wheel of the whole thing, the driver wrote in February, was one station and three days of counting; wheel, he said, is either the seat at the far platform or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ wheel I remember is the ring counted in the timetable, which closed in 1966 and is still counted as the quietest in the station. A ⑩ wheel, my mother said in 1968, is the only ring that improves by being counted; every wheel, she said, is a motion that has agreed to look like a ring. She said the motion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 轮子（指车站里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 轮子（指那个轮子本身，与薄薄的车票相对）
C. 固定搭配：turn the wheel 转动这一个轮子
D. n. 轮子（指留给孩子们订的那一个）
E. n. 轮子之事（抽象总称，指一处车站的轮子之事）
F. n. 轮子（指时刻表里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 轮子、转动（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 转动（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: turned the wheel that no passenger in the station would have counted
The wheel, meaning the ring itself and not the ticket
the wheel at the far platform
the wheel was the whole of the matter
the wheel had become a line in a timetable
The wheel of the whole thing
A wheel, my mother said in 1968

answers.why: turn the wheel 意为“转动这一个轮子”，1959 年那位司机把车站里没有一位乘客肯清点的一个轮子做了一遍。
wheel 意为“轮子”，指那个轮子本身而不是薄薄的车票，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被清点。
wheel 意为“轮子”，指车站里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张薄薄的车票。
wheel 意为“轮子”，指最远那座站台的留给孩子们订的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
wheel 意为“轮子、转动”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个转动就是那件事的全部。
wheel 意为“转动”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个轮子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
wheel 意为“轮子”，指时刻表里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1964 年这一个成了时刻表里的一行。
wheel 意为“轮子之事”，司机二月写道，整件事的轮子之事是一处车站和三个日子的清点。
wheel 意为“轮子”，我记得的是时刻表里清点过的那一个，1966 年到站了，至今仍被说成车站里最安静的一个。
wheel 为抽象总称，母亲 1968 年说，轮子是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的轮子。
